Rashi on Niddah 61a:12:1.english: To ground as smooth as a fingernail - To smooth ground that was never sown.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:13:1.english: The place of impurity was moist - For the water of the sheet was absorbed there, since the earth was soft.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:14:1.english: By the hand of Gedaliah - This implies that they were killed through Gedaliah.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:15:1.hebrew: יוחנן בן קרח - אמר לו לגדליה, שמעתי שבא ישמעאל בן נתניה להרגך (ירמיהו מ׳:י״ד):
Rashi on Niddah 61a:15:1.english: Johanan, son of Kareah - He said to Gedaliah: "I have heard that Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, is coming to kill you" (Jeremiah 40:14).

Rashi on Niddah 61a:16:1.hebrew: מיחש ליה מיבעי - ושמא הרגתם, ואסור להציל אתכם:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:16:1.english: One is required to be concerned about it - And perhaps you killed [someone], and it is forbidden to save you.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:18:1.hebrew: בני אחיה - שבא משמחזאי ועזאל, שני מלאכים שירדו בדור אנוש:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:18:1.english: The sons of Ahijah - Who came from Shamhazai and Azael, two angels who descended in the generation of Enosh.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:19:1.english: From the response to that righteous one - The Holy One, blessed be He, needed to respond [to him] that he should not fear him.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:1:1.hebrew: כאילו הן ראויות - לראות, ושתיהן טמאות, דמכל מקום דם מבינייהו נפיק:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:1:1.english: As though they were fit - To see [blood], and both of them are impure, for in any case, blood emerged from between them.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:20:1.hebrew: עוג פלט מן המבול - שברח לא"י, כדאמרינן בחלק:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:20:1.english: Og escaped from the flood - For he fled to the Land of Israel, as we say in [chapter] Chelek.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:21:1.hebrew: שאבד בו כתם - כגון שנכנס במים או נגלל בדם בהמה, ואין נודע מקום הנדות, וקי"ל במתני': אין דם הנדות טהור בלא שבעה סממנין:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:21:1.english: In which a stain was lost - For example, where [the garment] entered water or was rolled in animal blood, and the location of the menstrual [blood] is not known; and we maintain in the Mishnah: Menstrual blood is not purified without seven substances.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:21:2.english: One applies [to it] seven substances - Onto the garment.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:21:3.hebrew: ומבטלו - לדם. והאי דנקט הך ברייתא הכא, משום דאיירי לעיל בגלים שאבדה בהם טומאה ואין ידוע מקומה:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:21:3.english: And nullifies it - [This refers to] the blood. And the reason that [the Gemara] cites this baraita here is because it dealt above with heaps in which ritual impurity was lost and its location is not known.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:2:1.hebrew: חיצונה - קרי להך דלצד דרך עליית המטה. פנימית, אותה שלצד הקיר. ובגמרא מפרש: מאי שנא הכא דמפליג בין נמצא תחת הפנימית לנמצא תחת אמצעית, וברישא קתני: תחת אחת מהן כולן טמאות, אפילו נמצא תחת פנימית או חיצונה:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:2:1.english: The outer one - [The mishna] calls [by this term] the one on the side from which one gets into bed. [And] "the inner one" [refers to] the one on the side of the wall. And in the Gemara, it explains what is different here, that it distinguishes between [blood] found beneath the inner [woman] and [blood] found beneath the middle [woman], whereas in the first clause [the previous mishna] it teaches: "Beneath one of them, all of them are ritually impure," even if it was found beneath the inner or outer [woman].

Rashi on Niddah 61a:3:1.hebrew: אימתי - אמרו נמצא תחת חיצונה פנימית טהורה? בזמן שעלו דרך מרגלות המטה, דלא עברה פנימית על מקום מציאת הדם:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:3:1.english: When - [When did] they say [that if blood was] found beneath the outer one, the inner one is pure? When they went up via the foot of the bed, for the inner one did not pass over the place where the blood was found.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:3:2.hebrew: אבל עברו - שלשתן דרך עלייה, שהן דורסות ועוברות על החיצונה, כולן טמאות, ואפי' פנימית, דשמא כשעברה פנימית דרך שם נפל ממנה:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:3:2.english: However, they passed - [If] all three of them [passed] by way of climbing up, in that they step and pass over the outer woman, all of them are ritually impure, and even the inner woman, as perhaps when the inner woman passed that way, [the blood] fell from her.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:4:1.english: An impure heap - That there was an olive-bulk of a corpse there.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:6:1.hebrew: לבתולה - קרקע בתולה, ואם לא מצא, הגל טהור:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:6:1.english: To virgin [soil] - Virgin soil, and if he did not find [the impurity], the pile is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:7:1.hebrew: מאי שנא רישא - דקתני לעיל: נמצא דם תחת אחת מהן כולן טמאות, ולא מפליג בין נמצא תחת אמצעית לנמצא תחת פנימית או חיצונה:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:7:1.english: What is different in the first clause - For it taught above: "If blood is found beneath one of them, they are all ritually impure," and it does not distinguish between [whether] it was found beneath the middle one and [whether] it was found beneath the inner or outer one.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:7:2.hebrew: א"ר אמי רישא במשולבות - תכופות ודבוקות יחד. הלכך, אפילו נמצא תחת הפנימית, איכא לספוקי נמי בחיצונה:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:7:2.english: Rabbi Ami said: The first clause [deals with women who were] intertwined - [They were lying] close and clinging together. Therefore, even if [blood] was found beneath the inner [woman], there is reason to suspect the outer [woman] as well.

Rashi on Niddah 61a:9:1.hebrew: מאי שנא בדם דלא פליגיתו - דמודים אתם לי דהיכא דנמצא שלשתן טהורות, כולן טמאות:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:9:1.english: What is different regarding blood, that you do not disagree - For you agree with me that where all three of them were found [to be] pure, they are all impure:

Rashi on Niddah 61a:9:2.hebrew: ובגל - אתם חלוקים עלי, דאם בדק ולא מצא — טהור, ואע"ג דמוחזק לן דהואי טומאה בחד מינייהו:
Rashi on Niddah 61a:9:2.english: And with regard to a pile - You disagree with me, [maintaining] that if one examined [it] and did not find [anything, it is] ritually pure, even though it is established for us that there was ritual impurity in one of them.

Tosafot on Niddah 61a:13:1.hebrew: מקום טהרה לח - אסדינים קאי, דמתוך שהיה הקרקע קשה, לא בלע מים שבהסדינין, ומקום הטומאה יבש. ואית ספרים דגרסינן איפכא: מקום טומאה לח, ואקרקע קאי, שהיה לח מחמת הסדינין שבלע, לפי שהיה רך ותיחוח. וכה"ג בדק רבי יוחנן בן זכאי כשקצץ תורמוסי תרומה בעובדא דרבי שמעון בן יוחי במסכת שבת (דף לד.):
Tosafot on Niddah 61a:13:1.english: A place of purity [was] moist - [This] refers to the sheets, for since the ground was hard, it did not absorb the water that was in the sheets, and [at] the place of impurity [the sheets were] dry. And there are books that read the opposite: "A place of impurity [was] moist," and [this] refers to the ground, which was moist on account of the sheets, as it absorbed [their water] because it was soft and loose [earth]. And in a similar manner, Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai examined [the ground] when he cut lupines of teruma in the incident of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai in Tractate Shabbat (34a).

Tosafot on Niddah 61a:17:1.hebrew: אטמרינכו הא אמור רבנן האי לישנא בישא כו' - פי' בקונטרס: ושמא הרגתם, ואסור להצילכם. ובשאלתות דרב אחאי מפרש: שמא הרגתם, ואם אטמין אתכם, חייבתם ראשי למלך. והיינו מיחש מיבעי ליה למיחש: שיש לחוש ללשון הרע להאמינו לגבי זה, שיזהר שלא יבא לו הפסד, ולא לאחרים:
Tosafot on Niddah 61a:17:1.english: [If] I hide you, didn't the Rabbis say: This malicious speech, etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: And perhaps you killed [someone], and it is forbidden to save you. And in the She'iltot of Rav Achai it is explained: Perhaps you killed [someone], and if I hide you, you will have forfeited my head to the king [i.e., endangered my life with the king]. And that is [the meaning of] "one is required to be concerned about it": that one must be concerned about malicious speech [only to the extent of] believing it with regard to this — that he should be careful that no loss comes to himself, but not [to believe it so as to cause loss] to others.

Tosafot on Niddah 61a:20:1.hebrew: זה עוג שפלט מדור המבול - הכי נמי נפלט סיחון מדור המבול, כיון דאחי הוו; אלא דהך הפליט קים ליה דהוא עוג ולא סיחון מהאי טעמא גופיה, כיון דדחיל ליה משה. ועוד אמר (בפרק רבי אליעזר) (דף לד), שעוג מצאו לאברהם אבינו, שהיה עומד בגרנות לתקן עוגות לפסח, ועל שם זה נקרא עוג. ומייתי ליה משום דמחזי כלישנא בישא, דאמר במדרש: עוג אמר בלבו, אלך ואומר לאברהם וילחם וימות ואשא שרה אשתו; אפילו הכי, היה ירא משה שמא תעמוד לו זכות אברהם:
Tosafot on Niddah 61a:20:1.english: This is Og, who escaped from the generation of the Flood - Sihon as well escaped from the generation of the Flood, since they were brothers; rather, that this 'palit' [the fugitive] was known to him to be Og and not Sihon was for this very reason: since Moses feared him. And furthermore, it states (in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer) (page 34) that Og found our forefather Abraham standing at the threshing floors preparing cakes (ugot) for Passover, and on account of this he was called Og. And [the Gemara] cites this [incident here] because it resembles evil speech (lashon hara), for it says in the Midrash: "Og said in his heart: I will go and tell Abraham, and he will wage war and die, and I will marry Sarah his wife." Even so, Moses was afraid that perhaps the merit of Abraham would stand for him.

Tosafot on Niddah 61a:21:1.hebrew: מעביר עליו שבעה סממנין - וא"ת: ומה צריך להעביר עליו? הלא כיון שאבד ואינו ניכר, אינו מקפיד עליו ובטל ממילא, כדקתני ר' חייא לקמן (נדה דף סב:): דם הנדה ודאי מעביר עליו ז' סממנין ומבטלו, שכיון שהעביר עליו אזל ליה חזותא ואינו מקפיד עליו יותר, אע"פ שניכר, אלא בקפידא תליא מילתא. ויש לומר, דהכא קרי שפיר מקפיד עליו, דאם אינו מוצאו עכשיו, שמא ימצאנו פעם אחרת:
Tosafot on Niddah 61a:21:1.english: One applies seven substances to it - And if you say: Why does he need to apply [the substances] to it? Behold, since it was lost and is not discernible, he is not particular about it and it should become nullified on its own, as Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches below (Niddah 62b): "[Regarding] definite menstrual blood, one applies seven substances to it and nullifies it," for once he has applied [them] to it, its appearance is gone and he is no longer particular about it even though it is [still] discernible; rather, the matter depends on [whether one is] particular. And it may be said that here, he is rightfully considered "particular about it," for if he does not find it now, perhaps he will find it another time.

Tosafot on Niddah 61a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רבי אמי [רישא] במשולבות - פ"ה, רישא דלא מפליג איירי במשולבות ותכופות זו לזו, ולהכי איכא לספוקי בכולהו. ובהרבה ספרים לא גרסינן רישא. ואומר הר"י, דיש לפרש דסיפא איירי במשולבות, כלומר, מכוונות כל אחת במקומה, ולא היו תכופות ומעורבות זו בזו. ובפירוש ר"ח כתוב דמשלחפי שלחופי, שמתפרדות זו מזו:
Tosafot on Niddah 61a:7:1.english: Rabbi Ami said: [The first clause refers to] intertwined [women] - Rashi explained: The first clause, which does not distinguish, deals with [women who were] intertwined and close to one another, and therefore there is reason to be in doubt regarding all of them. And in many texts we do not read "the first clause" (reisha). And the Ri says that one can explain that the latter clause deals with [women who were] intertwined (meshulavot) — that is to say, aligned each one in her place, and they were not close together and intermingled with one another. And in the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel it is written: "that they were staggered" (de-meshalḥafei shalḥufei), meaning that they were separated from one another.
